behaviors.behavior: When a specialization hint specifies a block size equal to the whole tensor shape (one block covers the whole tensor), SparTA uses an existing general sparse kernel implementation (e.g., cuSPARSE, taco) instead of a specialized kernel.
behaviors.precondition: Specialization hint specifies block size equal to the tensor's shape (one block covers the whole tensor).
search_terms: block size equal to tensor shape

evidence.quote: A specialization hint could also specify the block size equal to the tensor’s shape (i.e., one block covers the whole tensor). In this case, SparTA can directly use the existing state-of-the-art general sparse kernel implementation (e.g., cuSPARSE [3], taco [53])

behaviors.behavior: When a specialization hint specifies a block size equal to the whole tensor shape, SparTA may use the dense kernel implementation if it performs better than the general sparse kernel.
behaviors.precondition: Block size equals whole tensor shape; dense kernel performs better.

evidence.quote: or even use the dense kernel implementation if it perform better.

behaviors.behavior: SparTA's specialization framework is general enough to incorporate any sparsity-aware techniques, including off-the-shelf sparse kernels and even their dense versions.
behaviors.precondition: Framework-level capability; applies when integrating external kernels.

evidence.quote: SparTA’s specialization framework is general to incorporate any sparsity-aware techniques, including the off-the-shelf sparse kernel and even its dense version.
